input.productDescription: A monitoring dashboard for the site reliability engineers of a company that runs a consumer payments app. The on-call engineer keeps it open all day and during live outages to see which services are degraded, the active incidents with severity, owner, and age, recent deploys, and the key metrics (error rate, latency, traffic) for each service. It must answer 'is anything broken, and what changed?' within seconds of looking at it. One responsive page for phones and desktops.
audience: engineering managers glancing at service health
primaryTasks: Tell within seconds whether anything is broken
See which services are degraded and how badly
Scan active incidents by severity, owner and age
Correlate recent deploys with changes in service health
Read error rate, latency and traffic per service
avoid: decorative gradients, glassmorphism or neon cyberpunk glow
alarm-red everywhere so that real severity does not stand out
oversized KPI cards with little information
motion that distracts during an outage
constraints: Vite + React + plain CSS only; no UI kits, component libraries or Tailwind
Must be readable on a phone held by someone paged at night and on a wall-mounted desktop display
Open for many hours: low visual fatigue, supports prefers-color-scheme
No external image URLs; no stock photos
